description: An underwriting manager must decide whether to grant a temporary covenant waiver to a logistics company and finalize the waiver's expiry, prepayment, documentation, and monitoring conditions, with input from risk, legal, relationship coverage, and loan operations.

shared_context.S1: HarborRoute Logistics has breached its quarterly minimum debt-service coverage ratio covenant and requests a temporary waiver while it completes a contract transition.
shared_context.S2: The existing loan agreement requires a minimum debt-service coverage ratio of 1.20.
shared_context.S3: The borrower has made all scheduled interest and principal payments on time, and the requested waiver is intended to cover one reporting period.
shared_context.S4: Maya makes the binding underwriting decision.
shared_context.S5: Bank policy requires a recorded pre-decision roundtable with risk, legal, relationship coverage, and loan operations before a covenant waiver can be finalized.

PF1.text: Jonah's review this morning confirmed that a one-time contract-transition charge caused the covenant breach; the applicable risk exception permits a waiver only with a temporary DSCR floor of exactly 1.05 and an expiry date of 2026-09-30. He has not yet attached the review to the credit file.

PF2.text: Elena received the executed legal drafting note yesterday, which requires the document to be a limited waiver with no release of other defaults and no increase in the facility commitment; the note has not yet been circulated to underwriting.

PF3.text: Marcus confirmed with the borrower this morning that HarborRoute will make a principal prepayment of exactly 600000 USD by 2026-08-15 as a condition of requesting the waiver; he has recorded this in his client call notes but has not uploaded them.

PF4.text: Nadia confirmed this week that loan operations can place the account on weekly covenant reporting, and the risk-exception workflow requires a weekly reporting package throughout the waiver; the workflow update is not yet reflected in the servicing system.

acceptance_conditions: The covenant waiver must be approved.
The temporary DSCR floor must be exactly 1.05.
The borrower must be required to make a principal prepayment of exactly 600000 USD.
The waiver must be documented as a limited waiver with no release of other defaults and no increase in the facility commitment.
Weekly covenant monitoring must be required.
The principal prepayment and weekly monitoring must be recorded as commitments.

content_checks.C5: decisions['waiver_document_type'] == 'limited waiver' and decisions['other_defaults_released'] == False and decisions['facility_commitment_increased'] == False
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'principal_prepayment' and c['target'] == 'HarborRoute Logistics' and c['detail'] == '600000 USD by 2026-08-15' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any(c['type'] == 'weekly_covenant_monitoring' and c['target'] == 'loan operations' and c['detail'] == 'weekly covenant reporting throughout the waiver' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The shared file shows only the original 1.20 covenant and one reporting period, while PF1 changes the required temporary floor to exactly 1.05, fixes the expiry at 2026-09-30, and supplies the risk basis that must be cited.

Without PF2, the settlement could use a general waiver and leave other defaults or the facility commitment unrestricted; PF2 changes the document to a limited waiver with no release and no commitment increase.

The borrower appears current on payments but has no confirmed cure in the shared file; PF3 changes the conditional approval to require an exact 600000 USD principal prepayment by 2026-08-15 and requires that exact prepayment commitment to be recorded.

The shared facts provide no monitoring cadence or operational confirmation; PF4 changes the waiver conditions to weekly covenant reporting throughout the waiver and requires that exact monitoring commitment to be recorded for loan operations.
